sources.what: General person detector with a multi-object tracker. Not in the reference list.
sources.use: Our player tracker on all 11 sets. Weak spots: far-side players hidden behind near ones, and many id switches.

work.title: Player tracks on all 11 sets
work.result: players.csv for every set; feeds the side heat maps, team sides and the serving end.

work.title: Fix: spectators above the floor's horizon were counted as near-end servers
work.result: On the 0.5 m Brunel away camera, feet on the far balcony map behind the camera (court y −18 to −124 m), i.e. behind the near baseline, so nearly every serve looked like ours. Feet past the horizon now get no court position.

work.title: Two more court-mapping traps found with the real scores
work.result: People more than 9 m behind a baseline (benches, the far wall) were counted as servers; a jump server's feet in the air map to the far end on a low camera. Servers are now looked for within 9 m of a baseline and placed where they stood in the second before the contact.

sources.use: Planned for better player tracking (fewer id switches). Needs a CodaLab account: sign up yourself, then Participate → Get Data.

work.title: Blocked: needs your CodaLab account
work.result: The data is behind a CodaLab competition sign-up (Participate → Get Data). Once you have it: train ByteTrack/MixSort-style association on its volleyball clips to cut id switches, which per-player stats need.

sources.name: VolleyVision (Roboflow sets)
sources.licence: AGPL-3.0 (repo LICENSE; README says CC BY-NC-ND)
sources.what: Player, ball, action and court-segmentation image sets, mostly from other camera angles.
sources.use: Action detector checks whether the receivers played each serve (hint only); its ball model is the most precise on Kent 2; its player model misses far players.

work.title: Action detector (YOLOv8m): did the receivers play the serve?
work.result: Run after every serve in all 11 sets (vball serving). It sees the far team, facing the camera, well (passes and spikes) and the near team's backs poorly. Against your 40 serve results on Kent 1 it is not reliable enough to decide: a receiver catching an out ball looks like a pass. Kept only as a hint for serves to check.
work.caption: Kent 3, longest rally: far-side passes ('defense') and attacks ('spike') found; near-side set barely (0.17).

work.title: Ball detector (YOLOv7-tiny, single images)
work.result: Best precision and recall of any model on Kent 2, weaker on the low Brunel away camera. Single images, so no tracking yet.

work.title: Player detector (YOLOv8m) for the serving end
work.result: Missed most far-end players, so nearly every serve looked like the near end's: 19 / 36 serving ends right on Kent 3 (YOLO11 tracks: 34 / 36). Not used.

work.title: Its trajectory fusion: the ball decides on low cameras
work.result: On the 0.5 m Brunel away camera players cannot show the serving end: the far court is a few pixel rows deep (a foot 19 px above the far baseline maps to 93 m) and jump servers' feet in the air map to the far end. sources.name: passform
sources.what: Ball trajectory turn → contact frame → nearest player = passer, then pose angles.
sources.use: Contact = a split between two fitted flights; toucher = the nearest wrist (YOLO11m-pose). First step to per-player touches.

work.title: Its touch rule with YOLO11m-pose on Kent 3
work.result: 226 contacts on Kent 3 (splits between fitted flights): a wrist was within 0.3 body heights of the ball at 42% of them. Those touches give legal visits (3 or fewer touches per side) 97% of the time (visits of 1, 2, 3, 4 touches: 40, 16, 5, 2). The examples look right (setters, attackers, servers); about half of the contacts still have no wrist close enough.
work.caption: Kent 3 contacts (yellow ring = ball at the flight split) and the player whose wrist is nearest: blue near end, red far end.
